name: Tournaments with small largest transitive subtournaments
description: construct() -> 190 integer bits, one for each pair (i,j), i<j, in lexicographic order on 20 vertices. Bit 0 orients i to j and bit 1 orients j to i. Minimize the exact largest transitive induced subtournament, computed by source-vertex subset recursion. The local n=20 task minimizes the largest transitive subset rather than reproducing the larger R(7) computation. This small order is labelled rediscovery, with no new-bound claim.

state_of_the_art.statement: Every tournament on n vertices contains a transitive subtournament on floor(log2 n) + 1 vertices (Stearns), which is 5 for n = 20. The Paley tournament on 23 vertices restricted to 20 vertices has no transitive subtournament on 6 (scripts/check_state_of_the_art.py). The largest tournament without one has 27 vertices (Sanchez-Flores; confirmed by Neiman, Mackey and Heule). Erdős Problem #1216 was answered negatively by Reid and Parker.
